On loans below $ 3,000, the usury limit is 16%. On loans above $ 3,000, the limit appears to be 5% per month. As to loans below $250,000, the interest rate must be specified in simple interest and in writing.
There is a provision for a variable rate, which is 16% or the T-Bill rate for non-competitive T-Bills.

Usury rate is 12%, or four points above the average T-Bill rate. Judgments bear interest at the rate of 12% or the lawful contract rate, whichever is higher.

The judgment rate is the "secondary market yield" for one-year T-Bills.

Usury rate is 4% greater than the Federal Reserve rate or 19%, whichever is less. On loans above $15,000, there is no limit. Judgments bear interest at the rate of 12% compounded yearly, or at such rate as is set by the Court.
The judgment rate is 9% or the contract rate, if lawful, whichever is higher. The general usury rate for loans below $50,000 is 12% or 5% above the discount rate for commercial paper.
Consumer loans may not exceed 10% unless the person is licensed to make consumer loans. Maximum rate on non-consumer loans is 45%. The judgment rate is the T-Bill rate plus 4%.
In civil suits where interest is allowed, it is allowed at 10%.
Judgments bear interest at the rate of 12% or a lawfully agreed upon rate.
Consumer transactions are governed at a maximum rate of 12%.
Usury rate is 5 to 17%. Judgments bear interest at the rate of 10% per annum, or the lawful agreed-upon rate, whichever is greater.
Judgments bear interest at 4% above the federal discount rate. On consumer transactions, the maximum rate of interest for the first $1,000 is 18%, above $1,000 is 14.45%.

Usury rate is 10% or more than 5% above the federal reserve rate. There is no usury limit on commercial loans above $5,000. The judgment rate is 9% or a rate legally agreed upon in the underlying obligation.
Judgment rate is fixed by the court.
Judgments bear interest at the rate of 5% above the U.S. Treasury securities rate.
Accounts bear interest at the rate of 12%. Judgments bear interest at the rate of 1% above a bond yield equivalent to T-bill auction price.
Judgments below $30,000 bear 15%; otherwise, they bear interest at the 52-week average discount rate for T-Bills, plus 4%.
Usury rate is 6% greater than New York City banks' prime rate. Judgments bear interest at the rate of 10% per annum.
Usury rate is 21% or the interest rate charged for T- Bills plus 9%. Judgment rate is 12%.
